items.followUp: Give two reasons why classification is useful in the study of organisms.

rubric.why: Identifying organisms is one main aim of classification.
rubric.description: States that classification helps identify organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying organisms as an aim.

rubric.why: Grouping organisms makes them easier to study.
rubric.description: States that classification groups organisms to make their study easier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that grouping makes organisms easier to study.

modelAnswer: It arranges organisms into groups, making them easier to study.

items.followUp: What is simple diffusion, and how does it differ from facilitated diffusion?

rubric.why: Facilitated diffusion is passive movement down a concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States that substances move passively from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the passive, downhill movement.

rubric.why: Facilitated diffusion occurs through proteins in the cell membrane.
rubric.description: Identifies membrane channel or carrier proteins as the route of transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the membrane proteins involved.

modelAnswer: Facilitated diffusion is the passive movement of substances across a cell membrane from a higher concentration to a lower concentration.
The substances pass through channel or carrier proteins in the membrane, and no cellular energy is used.
